//: Files Semgrep cannot fully parse (#2842, emptied of everything rewritable by
#3318). Every entry is a file the blocking scan reads only in part, so part of
it is NOT covered by any rule. Every one is a test file.
This list is a RATCHET enforced by scripts/ci/check-semgrep-coverage.mjs: a
file that becomes partly unparsed and is not listed fails the build, and a
listed file that starts parsing fully ALSO fails the build. Deletion is
forced by the gate; an addition only has to survive review, so the
guarantee is that this list never grows SILENTLY, not that it never grows.
WHAT MAY BE ADDED HERE IS NOW ALMOST NOTHING. Two of the three parser faults
are banned by `scan/no-semgrep-unparsable-import-type` in eslint.config.mjs:
an `import()` type in a call's type argument, and one in a function parameter
annotation. Both have a remedy available everywhere and changing no
behaviour, so a partial parse of either shape means the lint rule was
bypassed rather than that an entry is warranted. The three faults are stated
once, as the rule rather than as a spelling, in KNOWN_CONSTRUCTS in that
script - which is also the text the gate hands you when it fires. They are
NOT restated here.
NO COMPOSITION SUMMARY LIVES HERE ANY MORE, deliberately. The one that did
said '165 carry a generic call whose type argument contains an import() type,
and the remaining 4 are the string-literal ampersand'. The first clause is
gone entirely (#3318 rewrote all 165), and the second was wrong when written:
it counted four ampersand files where the gate's own message said three,
because one of the four was unparsed for the CALL shape and its own `&` never
tripped anything. A summary of a list is a second statement of the list, and
it drifted exactly as INV-SSOT-001 says it will. Each entry now carries its
own `reason`, which the gate REQUIRES - an entry with no reason is refused.
minimumScannedFiles is a coarse tripwire, NOT a ratchet: it catches a whole
directory falling out of scope through a new --exclude or .semgrepignore
entry, which the file list above cannot see. It is not a guarantee — a change
that excludes a directory and lowers the floor together passes everything, and
review holds that direction just as it holds an addition to this list.
This list doubles as the gate's canary: the only report that passes must name
exactly these files as partially parsed AND clear the floor, which a broken or
forged scan cannot do from either side.
Background: docs/MAINTENANCE.md -> "Semgrep parse coverage".

files.reason: A bare `&` inside a STRING literal, not JSX text: the prop value `currentXeroPath="/admin/xero?section=contactSync&view=failed"`. `&` is the remedy for JSX text only - writing it here would change the value the component receives, and the query string is the point of the case.

The same fault, in a long URL query built as a string constant and passed as `currentSearch`. Every `&` in it separates two parameters the dashboard has to read back, so escaping any of them would change what is under test.

The same fault, and the one that proves the remedy is unavailable: `href="/admin/bookings?sortBy=total&sortDir=desc"` is asserted with `toHaveAttribute` against that exact string, so rewriting the `&` changes the value the test asserts rather than only the source.
